Managed by Home runtime parameters or GEO settings. Optional resources follow their Home injection switch and merge strategy; when off, the source value may remain. This local field stays read-only.

Managed by the Android VPN session or external UI settings. Some desktop-only fields are unsupported. Showing this entry reveals its structure, not a current value, secret, or additional local override.
Managed through the local routing plan, strategy groups and rule sets. Edit those resources to change routing. The Home LAN bypass rules are applied afterward and remain at the beginning of rules.

The tree switch controls whether this field is included, independently of a boolean value of false. Applying a value keeps the current injection state; an unconfigured field stays off until enabled. Clearing removes its saved draft. Save the resource to commit changes, then restart an active VPN to apply them.

Click a parent name to expand it. Its switch enables or disables only configured, editable descendants, including those hidden by search. Partial selection is marked with a dash. A parent without configured children cannot be enabled in bulk. Values and merge strategies are retained when disabled.
DNS fields
Configure DNS resolvers, caching, fallback and resolution policies through nested dns fields.
Add local DNS overrides that are not already managed by Home, or show locked fields to inspect the available DNS structure.
A dns parent switch changes only configured local child fields. It does not toggle the runtime DNS service. Home-owned children stay locked and follow the final runtime injection settings.
Proxy node fields
Apply supported common settings to subscription proxy nodes. The * branch represents all applicable nodes, not a literal YAML key or a new proxy.
Adjust UDP, connection options or supported TLS fingerprints consistently across nodes.
Only applicable proxy nodes are changed. This tree does not fetch remote provider members or rewrite selector membership; do not enter * as a real proxy name.
Protocol sniffing fields
Configure HTTP, TLS and QUIC sniffing ports and destination overrides beneath sniffer.sniff.
Recover a domain from supported traffic when DNS or connection metadata is insufficient. Configure each protocol separately.
Protocol settings do not enable sniffer.enable automatically. Review port lists and destination overrides together to avoid unintended routing changes.
Android TUN fields
These fields describe the Android VPN interface. Jeemi manages its enable state, device and the TUN stack selected on Home.
Show locked fields to inspect the TUN structure. Use Home for supported runtime settings; Android handles routing and interface selection.
Local configuration cannot create another TUN or override the Home stack. Actual sessions use the VpnService descriptor and the saved stack selection; changes apply after a restart.
Controller fields
external-controller and its related fields describe API listeners, local IPC, TLS, browser origins and controller routing. Jeemi creates a private loopback listener for each VPN session.
Inspect the available controller structure when diagnosing API or external panel behavior. Android session settings determine the actual supported values.
Controller listeners and credentials are session-owned. Desktop IPC, exposed network listeners and custom controller routing are not local overrides on Android.
Controller authentication
secret is the authentication credential for the core controller API.
Jeemi generates and uses a private session credential for its controls and external panel. Local configurations do not supply or reveal it.
This entry is structural only. Do not put session credentials in local resources, exports or logs.
External UI fields
external-ui, external-ui-name and external-ui-url describe a controller web panel and its resources.
Manage the supported zashboard panel with the Home external UI switch. The verified local resources are prepared for the actual session.
Changing these source fields cannot override the panel managed by Jeemi. Prepare or disable the panel from Home and restart the VPN to apply the saved setting.
Runtime routing fields
rules contains ordered routing rules, proxy-groups contains selectors and strategy groups, and rule-providers contains named rule sources.
Use the local routing plan and linked groups or rule sets to rebuild or extend these structures while preserving resource references.
These entries cannot be edited as independent custom fields. Use the routing editor so referenced names and IDs remain valid; Home LAN bypass rules retain highest priority.
